content.title: LaMelo Ball fined $35,000, but not suspended for play that injured Bam Adebayo
content.text: The NBA fined Charlotte Hornets guard LaMelo Ball $35,000 for making “unnecessary and reckless contact” that “created a significant injury risk” to Miami Heat star Bam Adebayo in Tuesday’s Play-In Tournament game, the league announced Wednesday. Ball was also assessed a flagrant foul for the play, which resulted in an injury to Adebayo that sidelined him for the rest of the game.However, Ball was not suspended and will be available to play Friday when the Hornets face the Orlando Magic in a single-elimination game to advance to the playoffs.The incident occurred after Ball was bumped to the floor following his shot being blocked in the opening minute of the second quarter. As Ball lay on the ground, Adebayo jumped in the air and tossed the ball to Heat forward Pelle Larsson before landing out of bounds. After Adebayo landed near Ball, the Hornets star appeared to grab for one of Adebayo’s legs, and the Heat star fell hard to the floor on his lower back.The Heat eventually lost the elimination game 127-126 in overtime, with Adebayo unable to play the final two-plus quarters and overtime. Miami head coach Erik Spoelstra took exception to the play in the immediate aftermath of the game, saying that Ball should’ve been ejected for his actions.“I don’t think it’s cute. I don’t think it’s funny. I think it’s a stupid play. It’s a dangerous play,” said Spoelstra, whose team was eliminated from postseason contention for the first time in seven years. “I don’t think that belongs in the game. Tripping guys, those shenanigans.“He should have been thrown out of the game for that. … There’s just no place in the game for that.”Ball, who put up 30 points, 10 rebounds and five assists and made the game-winning basket, apologized for tripping Adebayo after the game.“I apologize on that one,” Ball said. “I got hit in the head, didn’t really know where I was. But I’m gonna check on him and see if he’s OK and everything.”In the pool report after the game, lead official Zach Zarba explained why that play could not be reviewed for a potential flagrant foul, despite Adebayo leaving the game with an injury.“Because play wasn’t stopped immediately, and there was no whistle on the play, the window to review the play was closed,” Zarba said. “Play was stopped after a change of possession, and then a timeout. So, by rule, our window to review that play then is closed.”Zarba went on to explain that while the officiating crew reviewed the play at halftime, their window for an in-game punishment had passed.The play echoed a similar incident on Jan. 14, 2024, in Miami, when Ball fell to the ground and reached out at one of Adebayo’s legs as the Miami big man ran up the floor. Adebayo managed to stay on his feet that time, and the Heat won that game 104-87.The $35,000 fine ties Ball’s second-largest fine in his six-year NBA career, matching one he received for making an obscene gesture during a game against the Heat in October. Ball was also fined an additional $25,000 for using profanity during a live postgame television interview Tuesday night. Connections: Sports EditionSpot the pattern.
